Agreement between DRP and specialist measurements was assessed by mean absolute error (MAE) and intraclass correlation coefficient. Diagnostic performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value. For patients who underwent surgery, 3-month postoperative recurrence was assessed.

Results

Among 952 participants (1904 eyes), the mean age was 27.9 years (range, 3-86 years); 493 participants were female (51.8%) and 459 were male (48.2%). A total of 1862 eyes were included in MRD1 analysis and 1830 eyes in LF analysis after quality control. DRP demonstrated high agreement with specialist measurements for MRD1 (MAE, 0.52 mm; 95% CI, 0.50-0.54 mm) and LF (MAE, 0.95 mm; 95% CI, 0.91-0.98 mm). For diagnosing ptosis, DRP achieved an AUC of 0.97 (95% CI, 0.96-0.97). For identifying surgical approach, DRP achieved an AUC of 0.98 (95% CI, 0.97-0.98). Performance remained consistent across sex, age, and geographic region. Among 206 surgical participants (248 eyes), the 3-month postoperative recurrence rate was 7.3% (95% CI, 4.4%-11.2%; 18/248 eyes), within the lower range of previously reported rates.

Conclusions and relevance

This study found that accurate, standardized quantitative blepharoptosis assessment might be supported by commercially available smartphones, demonstrating the potential of smartphone-based 3D reconstruction for external ocular assessment and clinical decision-making. Further studies are needed to evaluate its clinical impact.

records.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.

content.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.
content.abstract:
Importance

Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue.

Objective

To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay.

Design, setting, and participants

The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures

15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS).

Main outcomes and measures

Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated.

Results

Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.

records.title: Article- and Journal-Level Associations Between Altmetric Attention Scores and Citations in High-Attention Ophthalmology Publications.

content.title: Article- and Journal-Level Associations Between Altmetric Attention Scores and Citations in High-Attention Ophthalmology Publications.
content.abstract:
Importance

Altmetric Attention Scores (AAS) measure attention to scholarly articles through social media, news coverage, or policy citations. How AAS aligns with impact factors for ophthalmic peer-reviewed medical literature remains unclear.

Objective

To assess correlations between AAS and citation metrics at the article and journal levels.

Design, setting, and participants

This cross-sectional study included all citable items published between 2022 and 2023 in a subset of ophthalmology journals indexed in the 2024 Journal Citation Reports. The top 500 articles ranked by AAS were selected as a high-attention publication subset for detailed analysis.

Main outcomes and measures

The primary outcome was Spearman rank correlations between AAS rankings and normalized citation rankings (calculated as total citations divided by months elapsed since publication) at the individual article level and between an entire journal's AAS rankings and Journal Impact Factor (JIF) rankings.

Results

This study included 24 059 citable items in 99 journals. Among the top 500 high-attention articles, correlation between individual article-level AAS rankings and citation rankings was 0.08 (95% CI, -0.01 to 0.16; P = .08). At the journal level, correlation was 0.57 (95% CI, 0.41-0.69; P < .001). Correlations for predominantly clinical research-oriented journals compared with predominantly nonclinically or mixed research-oriented journals were 0.64 (95% CI, 0.46-0.79) vs 0.43 (95% CI, 0.09-0.69) (difference = 0.21; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.60; P = .24). Multivariable analysis showed that AAS rankings were independent of document type (review vs original article: β = -10.6; 95% CI, -47.8 to 26.6; P = .58) or publication date (per month elapsed: β = 0.7; 95% CI, -1.1 to 2.5; P = .45).

Conclusions and relevance

In this cross-sectional study of high-attention ophthalmology publications, individual article-level AAS rank was not associated with citation rank, whereas journal-level Altmetric rank was moderately associated with JIF rank and greater for clinical research-oriented journals. These findings suggest that online attention and impact factor reflect partially overlapping but distinct dimensions of research dissemination and that both metrics are independent, important variables that may contribute to judging the value of peer-reviewed medical journals.

records.title: Outcomes of As-Needed Aflibercept Treatment After Complete Regression in Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.

content.title: Outcomes of As-Needed Aflibercept Treatment After Complete Regression in Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.
content.abstract:
Importance

Complete polypoidal regression (termed regression) is a treatment goal in polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV), a common cause of vision loss globally. However, outcomes are controversial when treatments continue as fixed-dosing, treat-and-extend, or as-needed (PRN) regimens once regression is achieved.

Objective

To determine outcomes using PRN regimens after achieving complete polypoidal regression following an initial treatment of 3 or 6 monthly intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections in eyes with PCV.

Design, setting, and participants

This prospective cohort study took place at 4 university hospitals in Thailand. Eighty-one treatment-naive participants with PCV received 3 monthly aflibercept 2.0-mg injections. At week 12, eyes with regression underwent PRN treatment and follow-up monthly during year 1 and bimonthly during year 2. Eyes without regression at week 12 received 3 additional monthly injections and if regressed at week 24, also underwent PRN treatment and follow-up monthly through year 1 and bimonthly follow-up through year 2. Eyes without regression through week 24 received treat-and-extend regimens. These data were analyzed from August 2020 to September 2025.

Main outcomes and measures

Fluid-free interval between first visit with regression and first exudative recurrence on optical coherence tomography (OCT) by life-table analyses.

Results

Of 81 study eyes, mean [SD] age was 64 [8] years; 54% were female and 46% were male; 32 (40%) achieved regression at week 12 or 24. Of 26 eyes with regression, 13 (50%; 95% CI, 30%-70%) recurred within 2 years. Fluid-free probability after regression was 57% (95% CI, 37%-77%) at week 24 and 53% (95% CI, 33%-73%) at week 84. Among 14 eyes with recurrence, median best-corrected visual acuity change from the prior visit was -3.5 letters (IQR, -5.0 to -0.25); 3 (21%; 95% CI, 5%-51%) lost 10 or more letters, and 5 (36%; 95% CI, 13%-65%) had new hemorrhage. Post hoc exploratory analyses of eyes with complete polypoidal regression showed baseline massive subretinal hemorrhage had lower recurrence (hazard ratio [HR], 0.18; 95% CI, 0.04-0.80; P = .01). In contrast, leakage without subretinal hemorrhage may have had a higher hazard of recurrence (HR, 2.65; 95% CI, 0.89-7.94; P = .07).

Conclusions and relevance

In this study, half of the eyes with PCV achieved complete polypoidal regression remained quiescent after treatment deferral, whereas the remainder recurred. Posttreatment OCT biomarkers may help identify eyes that could benefit from continued treatment instead of PRN management.

records.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.

content.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Investigate the structure-function relationships between epiretinal membrane (ERM) stage, tractional abnormalities, and the gap area between the ERM and the retinal surface, in relation to visual acuity and quantitative contrast sensitivity function in patients with idiopathic epiretinal membrane.

Methods

This was a retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 111 participants diagnosed with idiopathic ERM. All patients underwent a comprehensive ophthalmologic examination, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography imaging using the SPECTRALIS Heidelberg system, and contrast sensitivity (CS) testing using the quantitative contrast sensitivity function method.

Results

Progressive stages of ERM were associated with declines in both CS and visual acuity (β* = -0.45 to -0.19, P < 0.02), with CS showing a more pronounced reduction than visual acuity, especially between controls and Stage 1. Ectopic inner foveal layer thickness exhibited a similar pattern of decline in both visual acuity (β* = 0.42, P < 0.001) and CS (β* = -0.46 to -0.18, all P < 0.02). By contrast, SUKIMA showed no significant association with any of the visual measurements assessed. Among the tractional abnormalities, the cotton ball sign correlated with diminished vision, particularly reflected by a notable drop in CS at the highest spatial frequencies tested with reduced CS at 12 cycles per degree (β* = -0.44, P = 0.02) and 18 cycles per degree (β* = -0.46, P = 0.02).

Conclusion

Quantitative contrast sensitivity function testing is particularly important for assessing visual function in ERM development, especially in the early stages.

records.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) using a novel deep learning-based approach, and to evaluate longitudinal changes following shunt surgery.

Methods

In this prospective study, 22 patients with iNPH and 22 age-matched healthy controls underwent peripapillary optical coherence tomography (OCT). A deep learning-based ResUNet model enabled choroidal segmentation and quantification of total choroidal area (TCA), stromal choroidal area (SCA), luminal choroidal area (LCA), and the choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Measurements were compared between groups and reassessed in iNPH patients after ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery.

Results

Forty-four eyes of 22 iNPH patients and 44 eyes of 22 controls were analyzed. iNPH eyes exhibited significantly greater mean SCA compared to controls (adjusted p < 0.05). On the other hand, CVI remained comparable between groups. Following a mean follow-up of approximately 12 months after shunt surgery, mean SCA showed significant reduction (adjusted p < 0.05), whereas CVI remained unchanged.

Conclusions

iNPH was associated with peripapillary choroidal changes, predominantly involving the stromal compartment. Deep learning-based OCT analysis may provide a noninvasive approach for quantifying peripapillary choroidal microstructure, although the clinical relevance of these findings remains to be established.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.

content.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Research on artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) is expanding, but integrated evidence on publication patterns, keyword trajectories, online search activity, and methodological characteristics remains limited.

Objective

To characterize AI-CDSS research by integrating bibliometric analysis, Google Trends comparison, and structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications.

Methods

Scholarly interest was assessed using bibliometric analysis of Web of Science records from 2016 through August 2026, including author-keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and reference co-citation, whereas Google Trends was used to characterize online search activity. A structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications was conducted to examine applications, methodological characteristics, and reported limitations.

Results

We analyzed 19,809 included publications from 2016 through August 2026. Output rose approximately 21-fold, from 193 records in 2016 to 4,082 in 2025. Output was geographically concentrated within the included corpus, with a Gini coefficient of 0.869. Among records with identifiable corresponding-author country or territory, China, the United States, and India accounted for 61.33%. Scientific Reports was the most frequent source (n = 916). Frequent artificial intelligence- and diagnosis-related keywords included machine learning (n = 5,666), deep learning (n = 4,022), and computer-aided diagnosis (n = 1,512). Bibliographic coupling identified 15 publication communities, and reference co-citation identified seven reference communities. In the monthly level-series comparison, 9 of 10 keyword concepts exhibited significant associations with Google Trends relative search interest, but none of the 10 first-difference associations remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Content analysis of 215 citation-ranked publications, including 191 empirical publications, showed frequent use of convolutional neural networks in diagnostic and radiology applications. Common limitations included limited external validation, infrequent calibration reporting, and sparse workflow-level or impact evaluation.

Conclusion

AI-CDSS research has rapidly expanded around machine learning, deep learning, and diagnostic applications, but the analyzed citation-ranked publications provide more evidence of methodological development than of clinical deployment. Integrating bibliometric, search-activity, and content-based perspectives shows limited short-term correspondence between online search activity and scholarly keyword use and highlights the need to move beyond model development toward independent external validation, prospective workflow and patient-outcome evaluation, calibration, fairness, and postdeployment monitoring.

records.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.

content.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training.

Methods

A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study.

Results

On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681.

Discussion

These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.

content.title: A review of deep learning applications on histopathologic and genomic data in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
content.abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis explains the histological pattern of injury seen through light microscopy in kidney biopsy specimens and is the end result of different injuries to podocytes. The clinical classification of patients by FSGS lesion is challenging because of a broad spectrum of etiologies, limited understanding of pathophysiology, and poor correlation among histopathology, treatment response, and clinical outcomes. Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is a problematic process to detect lesions, with low and late analysis of the absence of initial symptoms, and a challenging position of specific markers. However, Histopathological and genomic Data in Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) are significantly used in multiple research applications, but they face several limitations that restrict the efficiency of experimental analysis. This review systematically analyzed recent enhancements in biopsy-based analysis and deep learning models for FSGS, with specific emphasis on different mechanisms. Moreover, this review analyzed different strategies, namely kidney transplantation, pathogenesis to therapeutic approaches, transformer-based architectures, glomerular segmentation methodologies, multitasking strategy classification, and gene expression analysis for FSGS. This review analysis includes 121 research papers, which are selected and analyzed for glomerular segmentation, gene expression, clinical outcomes, lesion classification, and disease recurrence prediction. Based on the recent research frameworks, it explicitly states the performance analysis, benefits, as well as challenges of FSGS. The article presents details of a new dataset and future directions for improving the majority of nephropathology diagnoses previously available through the use of integrated approaches that utilize both histopathology and genomics, enhancing future research direction in FSGS.

records.title: Understanding the Inner Workings of Large Language Models in Medicine.

content.title: Understanding the Inner Workings of Large Language Models in Medicine.
content.abstract:
Background

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly influencing medical practice, education, and research. Their responsible integration into healthcare requires expertise in medical, ethical, practical, and theoretical domains.

Methods

We prompted GPT-o1 to generate examples illustrating how understanding transformer architecture can facilitate output interpretation. Key topics were extracted from its responses, and illustrative cases were identified and cross-checked against the peer-reviewed literature using Consensus.app, an AI-assisted literature-search tool.

Results

Five key topics were identified: (1) anticipating contextual focus in medical reasoning, (2) explaining "generic" or "textbook" responses, (3) understanding strengths and weaknesses in differential diagnosis, (4) explaining ambiguous or contradictory responses, and (5) identifying hallucinations in unfamiliar scenarios. Case examples highlight both benefits and limitations, including accurate attention to salient clinical details, reliance on generalized patterns, risks of base rate neglect in differential diagnosis, challenges of ambiguous prompts, and hallucinations in rare or underrepresented cases.

Conclusions

A theoretical understanding of LLMs is crucial for responsible clinical integration. Distinguishing between well-represented (short head) and underrepresented (long tail) knowledge, recognizing generic responses, and identifying hallucinations are essential competencies. Coupled with medical and ethical expertise, these skills will enable healthcare professionals to leverage LLMs effectively while mitigating risks.

records.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI), mainly AI-driven chatbots and large language models (LLMs) is reshaping dental education through adaptive, interactive, and simulation-based learning. While the transition in technology has been rapid, the evidence about the educational effectiveness of these technologies is still very diverse and not entirely directed.

Aim

To analyze the roles, educational effectiveness, and impact of integrating AI-driven chatbots and LLMs in dental education at the university level with a focus on learning outcomes and implementation practices.

Methods

The researchers conducted a thorough search of the electronic databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase for articles published from January 2018 to November 2025. This review met the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 criteria and was made up of original research articles on dental studentsand educators who were using AI-based chatbots as interventions. The outcomes measured were knowledge gain, clinical reasoning, diagnostic accuracy, communication skills, and engagement of learners. Due to the differences in the methodologies used the authors opted for a narrative synthesis approach.

Results

Six studies met the eligibility criteria and showed potential benefits of AI-driven chatbots and LLMs for diagnostic reasoning, learning performance, engagement, and individualized feedback although methodological and outcome heterogeneity limited direct comparison.

Conclusion

AI-driven chatbots and LLMs may complement university-level dental education, but their effectiveness and safe implementation require further rigorous evaluation.

records.title: Machine learning in prediction of epidermal growth factor receptor status in non-small cell lung cancer brain metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Machine learning in prediction of epidermal growth factor receptor status in non-small cell lung cancer brain metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations are present in 10-60% of all non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients and are associated with dismal prognosis. Lung cancer brain metastases (LCBM) are a common complication of lung cancer. Predictions of EGFR can help physicians in decision-making and, through optimizing treatment strategies, can result in more favorable outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the predictive performance of machine learning (ML)-based models in EGFR status in NSCLC patients with brain metastasis.

Methods

On December 20, 2024, the four electronic databases, Pubmed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science, were systematically searched. Studies that evaluated EGFR status in patients with brain metastasis from NSCLC were included.

Results

Twenty studies with 3517 patients with 6205 NSCLC brain metastatic lesions were included. The majority of the best-performance models were ML-based (70%, 7/10), and deep learning (DL)-based models comprised 30% (6/20) of models. The area under the curve (AUC) and accuracy (ACC) of the best-performance models ranged from 0.765 to 1 and 0.69 to 0.93, respectively. The meta-analysis of the best-performance model revealed a pooled AUC of 0.91 (95%CI: 0.88-0.93) and ACC of 0.82 (95%CI: 0.79-0.86) along with a pooled sensitivity of 0.87 (95%CI: 0.83-0.9), specificity of 0.86 (95%CI: 0.79-0.9), and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) of 35.2 (95%CI: 21.2-58.4). The subgroup analysis did not show significant differences between ML and DL models.

Conclusion

ML-based models demonstrated promising predictive outcomes in predicting EGFR status. Applying ML-based models in daily clinical practice can optimize treatment strategies and enhance clinical and radiological outcomes.

records.title: Applicator reconstruction in cervical cancer brachytherapy: A systematic review of current methods, challenges, and AI-driven future directions.

content.title: Applicator reconstruction in cervical cancer brachytherapy: A systematic review of current methods, challenges, and AI-driven future directions.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Accurate applicator reconstruction is a critical step in 3D image-guided brachytherapy (3D-IGBT) for cervical cancer, directly influencing tumor control and organ-at-risk sparing. This systematic review evaluates the accuracy, efficiency, and clinical impact of applicator reconstruction methods, focusing on AI's potential to overcome existing limitations.

Methods and materials

Following PRISMA guidelines, 23 studies from MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Lilacs and Web of Science (up to May 2025) were analyzed. Evaluation metrics included geometric accuracy (tip error, Hausdorff distance), reconstruction time, and dosimetric parameters (D90 HR-CTV, D2cc OARs). Methods assessed spanned manual (e.g., MPR, scout-based), semi-automatic (library method, clustering algorithms), and AI-driven approaches (e.g., U-Net, Dilated-Supervised Deep U-Net, Attention-Gated networks). Special focus was placed on deep learning (DL) architectures and their ability to overcome metallic artifacts, partial-volume effects, and inter-operator variability.

Results

Manual methods exhibited significant limitations, with tip errors reaching 4.1 mm. Semi-automated approaches reduced variability (library-based methods: <0.5 mm mean deviation) but remained constrained by predefined applicator models. AI-driven workflows demonstrated superior precision, achieving submillimeter accuracy (median tip error: 0.64 mm; Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) > 0.89) and dosimetric consistency (D2cc deviations <3%). Notably, DL models like DSD-UNet and Attention-Gated U-Net reduced reconstruction time to <30 s per case while maintaining robustness against CT artifacts. However, challenges persist, including limited clinical validation (60% of studies used phantoms), data heterogeneity (slice thickness: 0.6-5 mm), and generalizability to novel applicator designs.

Conclusion

AI-driven reconstruction reduces human-dependent errors and enhances efficiency, but clinical validation remains a priority. Reducing CT slice thickness (≤1.5 mm) and combining scout images to mitigate metal artifacts are recommended. Future research should focus on generalizable AI models for nonlibrary applicators and large-scale clinical validation.

records.title: Serum M2BPGi as a predictor of hepatocellular carcinoma development in chronic hepatitis B and C: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Serum M2BPGi as a predictor of hepatocellular carcinoma development in chronic hepatitis B and C: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) kills about 830,000 people each year, and most cases arise in chronic viral hepatitis. Better risk markers would let clinicians focus surveillance where it matters. Mac-2 binding protein glycosylation isomer (M2BPGi) is a serum glycobiomarker of liver fibrosis. Several cohort studies tie elevated M2BPGi to HCC. No quantitative synthesis has pooled this evidence across viral etiologies.

Methods

We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus through April 2026 for longitudinal studies that reported hazard ratios (HRs) for HCC linked to elevated M2BPGi in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) or C (HCV). We registered the protocol with PROSPERO. The primary pool restricted to longitudinal studies with categorical cutoffs that reported HRs. We used random-effects meta-analysis with restricted maximum likelihood and the Hartung-Knapp adjustment.

Results

Twenty-three publications (24 study entries) met inclusion criteria. The primary pool of 15 longitudinal categorical HR-reporting studies covered 12,161 participants and at least 1,189 HCC events. The pooled HR was 4.61 (95% CI 3.24-6.54; p < 0.0001) with low heterogeneity (I2 = 25.6%). The 95% prediction interval ran from 2.08 to 10.18. The effect held across etiology (CHB k = 5 HR 4.12; HCV k = 10 HR 5.07; p_subgroup = 0.62) and across measurement timing (baseline HR 3.21; on/post-treatment HR 5.62; post-SVR HR 5.45; p_subgroup = 0.23). Two sensitivity pools re-introducing OR-based studies gave HR 4.71 (k = 16) and HR 4.89 (k = 17). Egger's test was positive (p = 0.0003); trim-and-fill imputed six studies and pulled the adjusted HR to 3.53.

Conclusion

Elevated serum M2BPGi is strongly and consistently associated with HCC development in patients with chronic hepatitis B and C. The effect holds across etiology, treatment status, and measurement timing-including after sustained virological response. Funnel asymmetry suggests the true effect is closer to a 3.5-fold than a 4.6-fold risk increase, still large enough to matter clinically. M2BPGi is a credible candidate to layer onto current viral hepatitis surveillance, particularly for risk stratification after virological control.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261372566, identifier CRD420261372566.

records.title: Effectiveness of hyaluronic acid and its derivatives on diabetic foot ulcer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Effectiveness of hyaluronic acid and its derivatives on diabetic foot ulcer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

In this study, we aim to evaluate the effects of hyaluronic acid and its derivatives on wound healing in diabetic foot ulcer.

Methods

The electronic databases included PubMed, BIOSIS, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and Google Scholar internet. The final search was updated on Aug 31, 2024. We assessed eligible studies that comparing the effects of hyaluronic acid and its derivatives with other dressings on wound healing in diabetic foot ulcer. The primary outcomes included the rate of ulcers completely healed, time to healing and adverse event. The standard mean differences (SMDs) or the odds ratios (ORs) were calculated for continuous or dichotomous data, respectively. Data were analyzed by using the Cochrane Collaboration's RevMan 5.0 software.

Results

We assessed each included study with the Cochrane 'Risk of bias' tool. Seven RCTs involving 444 patients and 456 ulcers were included in our study. Hyaluronic acid may improve the complete ulcer healing rate (OR 3.92, 95% CI 1.74 to 8.81, P = 0.02, I2 = 62%) and shorten the time to ulcer healing (SMD = -0.83, 95% CI -1.13 to -0.53, P = 0.24, I2 = 28%), with no increasing the incidence of adverse events (OR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.46 to 1.35, P = 0.31, I2 = 16%).

Conclusion

In conclusion, HA and its derivatives could be a potentially beneficial therapy for DFU treatment that promotes the complete ulcer healing rate, shortens healing time, without increasing incidence of adverse events.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD42024588743, identifier CRD42024588743.

records.title: Explainable AI in kidney stone detection and segmentation: a mini review.

content.title: Explainable AI in kidney stone detection and segmentation: a mini review.
content.abstract: Kidney stones are one of the most common renal disorders that can produce severe complications if not diagnosed and treated early. Recently, advances in AI have ensured that deep learning and explainable AI enable the automatic segmentation and detection of kidney stones from medical imaging, thus improving diagnostic efficiency and accuracy. For this review, eighteen representative studies using machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid models for kidney stone segmentation were considered, which were published in the period between 2020 and 2025. The XAI techniques being mainly utilized with the discussed models in the study are SHAP, LIME, Grad-CAM, Layer-wise Relevance Propagation, and EigenCAM. Such approaches tend to enhance clinicians' trust in allowing early diagnosis and supporting clinical decision-making, especially in resource-constrained settings. Regardless of the towering results, this area still suffers due to certain limitations such as lack of diversity in datasets, absence of multimodal integration, and scarcity of real-world validation. All in all, integrating DL with XAI presents a transparent, reliable, and clinically acceptable approach to detecting and segmenting kidney stones.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Diagnosis of Tongue Cancer: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Diagnosis of Tongue Cancer: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract: Background: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is an aggressive oral malignancy characterized by early submucosal invasion and a high risk of cervical lymph node metastasis. Accurate and timely diagnosis is essential, but it remains challenging when relying solely on conventional imaging and histopathology. This systematic review aimed to evaluate studies applying artificial intelligence (AI) in the diagnostic imaging of TSCC. Methods: This review was conducted under PRISMA 2020 guidelines and included studies from January 2020 to December 2024 that utilized AI in TSCC imaging. A total of 13 studies were included, employing AI models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and Random Forest (RF). Imaging modalities analyzed included MRI, CT, PET, ultrasound, histopathological whole-slide images (WSI), and endoscopic photographs. Results: Diagnostic performance was generally high, with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.717 to 0.991, sensitivity from 63.3% to 100%, and specificity from 70.0% to 96.7%. Several models demonstrated superior performance compared to expert clinicians, particularly in delineating tumor margins and estimating the depth of invasion (DOI). However, only one study conducted external validation, and most exhibited moderate risk of bias in patient selection or index test interpretation. Conclusions: AI-based diagnostic tools hold strong potential for enhancing TSCC detection, but future research must address external validation, standardization, and clinical integration to ensure their reliable and widespread adoption.

records.title: Comparative efficacy of different durations and dosages of vonoprazan and amoxicillin dual therapy: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

content.title: Comparative efficacy of different durations and dosages of vonoprazan and amoxicillin dual therapy: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Background

The combination of vonoprazan and amoxicillin (VA) has been shown to be effective in eradicating Helicobacter pylori infection; however, the optimal treatment duration and dosage are yet to be determined.

Methods

A systematic literature search of PubMed, Embase, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure was performed to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing different durations of VA dual therapy or comparing this dual therapy with bismuth-containing quadruple therapy (BQT). All trials were conducted in China. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was used to evaluate the eradication rates and incidence of adverse events across different treatment regimens.

Results

Thirty-eight randomized controlled trials were ultimately included in the analysis. Network meta-analysis revealed that both the 14- and 10-day VA regimens achieved higher eradication rates compared with BQT, with odds ratios (OR) of 1.7 [95% credible interval (CrI) 1.3-2.1] and 1.4 (95% CrI 1.1-2.0), respectively. The 7-day regimen did not yield a difference in eradication rate compared with BQT (P > 0.05). All VA dual therapy regimens were associated with lower rates of adverse events than those for BQT. Among patients receiving the 14-day VA dual therapy regimen, there was no difference in eradication rates between the high- and low-dose groups. The low-dose 14-day regimen was associated with higher eradication outcomes than the low-dose 10-day regimen. No significant differences in adverse event rates were observed between the various dosage groups.

Conclusion

The 14-day low-dose VA dual regimen offered a favorable balance between efficacy and safety, suggesting that it may be a promising option for H. pylori eradication.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261284331, identifier: CRD420261284331.

records.title: Clinical assessment of the ocular surface, cornea and anterior segment: a critical review of diagnostic techniques and emerging technologies.

content.title: Clinical assessment of the ocular surface, cornea and anterior segment: a critical review of diagnostic techniques and emerging technologies.
content.abstract:
Background

The anterior segment and its adnexa, including the eyelids, tear film, cornea, sclera, conjunctiva, anterior chamber, aqueous humour, iris, ciliary body, and lens, play essential roles in ocular health and visual function. Clinical assessment of these structures should begin with a comprehensive examination using slit-lamp biomicroscopy, followed, when indicated, by more detailed evaluation with specialised imaging techniques.

Purpose

This narrative review provides a comprehensive overview of the clinical and imaging methods available for assessment of the anterior segment and its adnexa, ranging from conventional approaches, such as slit-lamp biomicroscopy, to advanced modalities including anterior segment optical coherence tomography, confocal microscopy, and digital imaging systems. Particular attention is given to recent technological advances, including high-resolution anterior segment imaging, automated meibography, and tear film analysis devices.

Discussion

This review highlights the clinical relevance, diagnostic value, strengths, and limitations of each technique, emphasising the importance of integrating complementary diagnostic tools to achieve accurate diagnosis, personalised management, and improved patient outcomes. Future perspectives: Finally, this review discusses emerging technologies and future perspectives, with particular emphasis on the integration of multimodal imaging and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches to further improve diagnostic accuracy, personalise clinical management, and optimise patient outcomes.

records.title: Recent applications of artificial intelligence in cancer radiotherapy and immunotherapy: current status and future directions.

content.title: Recent applications of artificial intelligence in cancer radiotherapy and immunotherapy: current status and future directions.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) enhances the precision, personalization, and efficiency of cancer treatment through deep learning and machine learning techniques. This review comprehensively examines the evolution of AI and its expanding applications in cancer radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and drug discovery and repurposing. In radiotherapy, AI enables automated medical image segmentation, thereby facilitating the accurate delineation of tumor targets. Furthermore, AI-driven feedback systems support clinicians in developing individualized treatment plans by offering real-time assessment of treatment safety and potential efficacy. In the context of cancer immunotherapy, AI integrates multi-omics data to advance the discovery of novel biomarkers, analyze the tumor immune microenvironment, and accurately predict responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Moreover, AI accelerates drug discovery and repurposing through virtual screening, protein structure prediction, and the identification of novel therapeutic targets. However, the true clinical value of these AI models depends heavily on their generalizability across diverse patient cohorts and their performance compared to standard clinical baselines. Despite these promising prospects, AI still faces challenges in clinical applications, such as insufficient data standardization, poor model interpretability, and a lack of ethical oversight, delaying its formal inclusion into standardized clinical guidelines. With the rapid growth of data volume and computational power, AI is expected to play an increasingly central role in cancer management, holding immense promise for improving patient outcomes and advancing precision oncology.

records.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis of emergency trauma outcomes: trends, interventions, and survival rates.

content.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis of emergency trauma outcomes: trends, interventions, and survival rates.
content.abstract:
Background

Trauma remains one of the leading global health challenges, with morbidity and mortality disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). While high-income nations have reported improved outcomes through the implementation of structured trauma systems, LMICs continue to bear the greatest burden of trauma-related deaths.

Objective

This meta-analysis evaluates the influence of trauma centers and organized trauma systems on reducing mortality among patients with traumatic injuries, irrespective of age, region, or mechanism of injury.

Methods

A meta-analysis was conducted of peer-reviewed studies published between January 2010 and December 2022, retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies included all age groups and trauma types, comparing outcomes between trauma centers/systems versus non-trauma settings, as well as pre- and post-implementation periods of trauma systems. Data were synthesized using relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Group A (trauma centers/systems vs. non-trauma centers/systems) reported a reduced mortality risk associated with organized trauma care (RR = 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.34; I2 = 89.37%). Group B (pre- vs. post-system implementation) showed a significant decrease in mortality following system introduction (RR = 1.87; 95% CI: 0.79-4.43; I2 = 99.55%). Funnel plot analyses indicated minimal publication bias.

Conclusion

Evidence supports the role of trauma centers and systems in significantly improving survival among trauma patients. However, persistent disparities remain, especially in LMICs and rural areas. Future research should emphasize long-term patient outcomes and strategies to reduce inequities in trauma care delivery.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Personalized Breast Cancer Drug Safety: From Preclinical Toxicology to Clinical Risk Management.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Personalized Breast Cancer Drug Safety: From Preclinical Toxicology to Clinical Risk Management.
content.abstract:
Purpose

The artificial intelligence (AI) implementation in personalized medicine has transformed drug safety, especially in breast cancer treatment. The importance of the need to treat breast cancer individually is acute as the disorder is heterogeneous and reacts differently to the use of chemotherapeutic agents.

Methods

Use of AI technologies including machine learning algorithms, deep learning, and predictive analytics can be used to acknowledge the presence of any possible toxicological risks in the early drug development stages to enhance efficacy and safety of therapies.

Findings

The strategies can be used to tailor treatment according to the genetic, molecular, and clinical features of a patient and minimize adverse drug reactions and maximize outcomes. The promise in the application of AI to predict treatment responses, optimize drug dosages, and ensure long-term safety through the combination of clinical trials, patient records, and real-world evidence has been high.

Implications

Throughout this review, it has been shown that AI can transform preclinical toxicology, clinical trial design, and postmarketing surveillance and overcome challenges and opportunities in the expanding area of drug development in breast cancer https://clinicaltrials.gov/.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiograms and Pregnancy-Related Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiograms and Pregnancy-Related Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Pregnancy-related cardiomyopathy (PRCM) is a leading cause of maternal death in the United States. PRCM symptoms often overlap with those of normal pregnancy and the lack of validated screening tools limits early recognition and contributes to diagnostic delays. Multiple artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiogram (AI-ECG) models have been developed and validated for PRCM detection.

Objectives

We sought to investigate the pooled diagnostic performance of these models.

Methods

A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane was performed to identify studies investigating the use of AI-ECG models for PRCM detection. Studies reporting complete 2×2 confusion matrix data for the AI-ECG model were included for analysis. Univariate and Reitsma bivariate random effects model meta-analysis was performed. Pooled performance estimates with 95% CIs are presented in forest plots and a summary receiver operating characteristics curve.

Results

Our search identified 716 studies (PubMed: 84, Scopus: 544, Cochrane: 88) from which 6 studies involving 2,928 patients were included in the meta-analysis. Univariate random effects model meta-analysis revealed a pooled sensitivity of 0.808 (0.656-0.902), specificity of 0.944 (0.889-0.973), and diagnostic OR of 54.017 (37.918-76.952). Following Reitsma bivariate random effects model meta-analysis, the AI-ECG models yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.775 (0.623-0.878); specificity of 0.936 (0.871-0.969); and area under the curve of 0.932 (0.813-0.953) for PRCM detection.

Conclusions
